facts.claim: The Green Revolution in India is linked to the loss of soil flora and fauna and ecological unbalance.
facts.quote: The country witnessed the benefits Green Revolution Technologies (GRTs) in boosting of grain yield and the after effect of GRTs during past few decades in terms of deterioration of soil fertility and land degradation, loss of soil flora and fauna, genetic erosion, ecological unbalance

facts.claim: The Green Revolution in India is linked to yield plateauing and associated insecurity in the livelihood of the farmers.
facts.quote: The country witnessed the benefits Green Revolution Technologies (GRTs) in boosting of grain yield and the after effect of GRTs during past few decades in terms of deterioration of soil fertility and land degradation, loss of soil flora and fauna, genetic erosion, ecological unbalance, yield plateauing and associated insecurity in livelihood of the farmers.

facts.claim: The Green Revolution in India is linked to the deterioration of soil fertility and land degradation.
facts.quote: The country witnessed the benefits Green Revolution Technologies (GRTs) in boosting of grain yield and the after effect of GRTs during past few decades in terms of deterioration of soil fertility and land degradation

facts.claim: The use of urea as a nitrogen-rich fertilizer in India is linked to global warming.
facts.quote: As urea, a nitrogen-rich fertilizer is used much more than the recommended 4-to-1 ratio to potassium; it is contributing to the global warming.

facts.claim: The Green Revolution in India is linked to systematic damages to the soil, groundwater, and ecosystem.
facts.quote: The extent of systematic damages caused in the process of Green Revolution to the soil, groundwater, and ecosystem needs to be quantified.
facts.causalWarning: causal wording, but the cited study only shows an association

facts.claim: The Green Revolution in India is linked to the degradation of soil health and increasingly larger shares of public spending on input subsidies.
facts.quote: Both continents have two challenges in common: degradation of soil health and increasingly larger shares of public spending on input subsidies.

research.angle: While the Green Revolution successfully boosted grain yields in India, it is linked to long-term soil fertility deterioration, land degradation, and ecological imbalance.
research.verdict: The sources provide evidence that Green Revolution Technologies are linked to significant environmental and soil degradation in India and other regions.
research.caveat: The sources do not provide a specific quantification of the systematic damages caused to the soil or groundwater.
